  • The updated release targets cleanroom readiness in October 2028 and mass production in H2 2029. About 1,000 operating staff are distinct from 7,000 direct and indirect jobs.
  • The older project homepage still advertises H2 2028 operations; the later detailed production schedule takes precedence.
  • City project information places site work north of Kalberer on Yeager Road. The marker is the nearby road intersection as site-area context, not a surveyed building centroid or the Purdue ceremony venue.
  • Published project-cost evidence: “a total expected investment of over $4 billion” The numeric cost uses the source currency without conversion; US$4 billion records a disclosed floor, not an exact final cost.

pin.longFormSummary:
• Avio’s first U.S. manufacturing plant is planned for thousands of tactical solid rocket motors annually. HITT leads construction, with completion targeted for late 2028 and production early in 2029.
  • The September operator release gives about 900,000 square feet and roughly 1,500 expected technical jobs. These are projections, not completed hiring or current output.
  • Virginia’s same-day announcement supports the $500 million project scale. No exact building centroid was verified, so the pin identifies the industrial park without guessed coordinates.
  • Published project-cost evidence: “new $500 million manufacturing facility” The numeric cost uses the source currency without conversion.
  • September 29, 2026 groundbreaking for the Hurt, Virginia solid rocket motor plant. Credit: Avio USA.

pin.longFormSummary:
• The new facility centralizes GMLRS solid rocket motor production and was designed to double current capacity. Opening does not establish that doubled output has already been achieved.
  • The disclosed $216 million cooperative agreement also covers Virginia facilities and Alabama upgrades. It is not a Camden-building construction price, so price and currency remain null.
  • The operator distinguishes this factory from other ongoing Camden expansions. No exact new-building footprint or parcel point was established; the industrial-park location is retained without guessed coordinates.
  • October 20, 2026 ribbon cutting at the Arsenal of Freedom solid rocket motor facility in Camden. Credit: L3Harris Technologies.

gaps: Bayer: exact factory parcel/coordinates and construction start day not established; announcement date is confirmed, 2031/2034 module dates are targets. Operator HTML403; city page and Manufacturing Dive rendering independently checked.

SK hynix: intersection marker is site-area context, not surveyed centroid. Homepage H2 2028 operations conflicts with newer August28 release specifying October2028 cleanroom and H2 2029 mass production. Project/construction galleries checked; maintenance image and stale schedule not used as fresh proof. Further permit/litigation audit remains outside this milestone batch.

Avio: exact plant parcel point not verified. Use September operator900000sqft/1500jobs projections rather than older February860000sqft/1000jobs. Completion late2028 and production early2029 are targets.
Fairfield: existing works coordinates only, not new building centroid; $475M Q&T excludes $75M Premium Thread Line. Ceremony photograph, not a completed-plant photograph.

L3Harris: exact new-building footprint and standalone budget unpublished. $216M covers three locations; not attributed to one factory. Investor mirror403/plain BusinessWire media download failed; direct operator photo downloaded with plain curl.

Novelis: first cold-mill coil is a commissioning milestone, not full commercial opening. Latest Oct7 release targets Q2 2027 shipments. Old homepage H2 2026 commissioning and17B cans differ in scope/timing from latest release; not silently treated as current shipment capacity. Address point is site context.
